title: Make the explainer site introduce Athena and fix newcomer findings
summary: Rework the generated explainer page so a newcomer at doodla.github.io/athena first learns what Athena is and that the page is an example study of firstmate. Add a next-step section, linked claim sources, and a plain-language f2 limit. The producer must run the gates and map each criterion to evidence before reporting.

defaults_applied.how: New site tests; cargo test, clippy and fmt must be clean.
Site is built and its HTML inspected.
Page copy written for an outside newcomer.
One focused change to the site generator and its study text.
Fix the framing in the generator and the study text rather than patching one string.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience is a newcomer arriving at the site.
Athena repo URL is https://github.com/doodla/athena; firstmate URL is taken from the study pin.
Source links point to files at the pinned commit on the firstmate repository host.
Study text edits may require regenerating or updating validation.json; edit it only if the validator requires.
The producer's final report includes a per-criterion evidence table and the results of the gate commands.

acceptance_criteria.text: In xtask/src/site.rs the page title and first heading name Athena, and an opening paragraph says what Athena is, that the page is an example of what its study capability produces, and that firstmate is the system studied. A named test asserts this.

The 'What firstmate is' text says who uses firstmate and that its workers are AI coding agents. The captain glossary entry says plainly who the captain is, or what the study does and does not establish, and is not only 'The text says no more about who the captain is.'

The page has a visible next-step section with anchor links to the Athena repository and firstmate's repository. Each claim source renders as an anchor to its file at the pinned commit, with link text HTML-escaped. Named tests cover the next-step links, the source links and the escaping.
The text for finding f2 in 'Limits of this study' no longer contains 'guard_evaluated_by for nobody' and is in plain language. A test asserts the phrase is absent from the rendered HTML.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. All pass with no warnings. Run `cargo test` for the study validation too.
Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site`. It writes target/site/index.html containing the Athena heading and the repository links, and `git status` shows no changes in the work tree from the build.
The final report has a table mapping each criterion to evidence (test name or HTML excerpt) and records the gate command results.

out_of_scope: Changing the study's claims or pin
Changing GitHub Pages workflow or deployment
Adding install or run tooling for firstmate
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
departures: Slightly lower verification pass rate and higher cost because the previous attempt failed on this multi-part list.
